newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Jewish leader joins Portugal gold probe group.
newsitem.headline: Jewish leader joins Portugal gold probe group.

text.p: Israel Singer, general secretary of the World Jewish Congress, has joined a special commission helping to investigate gold which Portugal received from Nazi Germany during World War Two, the country's central bank said on Friday.

A statement announced the appointment of Singer and a Portuguese academic, Professor Jaime Reis of the European Institute in Florence, as members of the three-man commission, headed by former president Mario Soares.
The group will accompany the work of economic historian Joaquim Costa Leite, who was appointed last December by the Bank of Portugal to investigate its gold dealings in the years 1937 to 1946.
"The board of the Bank believes that the Commission's work will be fundamental to attain the goals of total transparency and historical clarification," the statement said.
Neutral Portugal was the second largest buyer of gold from Nazi Germany after Switzerland during World War Two, giving rise to suspicions that some of the bullion bought was looted.

Nazi troops removed bullion from countries invaded during the war, including Belgium and Holland, and there is also the highly emotive question of what happened to gold -- watches, jewellery and even teeth -- stolen from concentration camp victims.

Portugal, which was ruled by a rightwing dictatorship at the time, says that the gold acquired during the war years was in payment for exports it was legally allowed to make as an officially neutral country to Germany and its allies.
